nodes.summary: A* leaves exactly the unreachable vertices at infinity. Let $G$ be a directed graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with natural edge weights $w$, let $h$ be any heuristic with natural values and let $s$ be a source vertex. The path weight $g(v)$ that A* from $s$ returns for a vertex $v$ is infinite if and only if $v$ is not reachable from $s$ in $G$.
nodes.title: A* leaves exactly the unreachable vertices at infinity

nodes.summary: A* with a consistent heuristic is optimal. Let $G$ be a directed graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with natural edge weights $w$, let $h$ be a consistent heuristic with natural values and let $s$ be a source vertex. If the path weight $g(v)$ that A* from $s$ returns for a vertex $v$ is finite, then $g(v) \le d$ for every weight $d$ of a path in $G$ from $s$ to $v$.
nodes.title: A* with a consistent heuristic is optimal

nodes.summary: A*'s finite path weights are realized by paths. Let $G$ be a directed graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with natural edge weights $w$, let $h$ be a consistent heuristic with natural values and let $s$ be a source vertex. If the path weight $g(v)$ that A* from $s$ returns for a vertex $v$ is finite, then some path in $G$ from $s$ to $v$ has weight exactly $g(v)$.
nodes.title: A*'s finite path weights are realized by paths

nodes.summary: A*'s predecessor edges are tight. Let $G$ be a directed graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with natural edge weights $w$, let $h$ be a consistent heuristic with natural values and let $s$ be a source vertex. If A* from $s$ records $u$ as the predecessor of a vertex $v$, then $G$ has an edge from $u$ to $v$, the path weights $g(u)$ and $g(v)$ that A* returns are both finite, and $g(v) = g(u) + w(u, v)$.
nodes.title: A*'s predecessor edges are tight

nodes.summary: A consistent heuristic that vanishes at the goal is admissible.
nodes.title: A consistent heuristic that vanishes at the goal is admissible

nodes.summary: For a directed graph $G$ with natural edge weights $w$, a heuristic $h$ with natural values is admissible for a goal vertex $t$ when it never overestimates the weight of a path to $t$: $h(v) \le d$ for every vertex $v$ and every weight $d$ of a path in $G$ from $v$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Admissible heuristic

nodes.title: Output of A-star search

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $w$ assign a natural number $w(u, v)$ to each pair of vertices. A heuristic $h$ assigning a natural number to each vertex is consistent (monotone) if $h(u) \le w(u, v) + h(v)$ for every edge $u \to v$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Consistent heuristic

nodes.summary: Given an A* result $r$ on $n$ vertices and a vertex $v$, follow the predecessor pointers of the underlying Dijkstra search backward from $v$, at most $n$ times, until the source is reached, and return the visited vertices in order from the source to $v$. There is no result if a vertex without a predecessor is met before the source, or if the source is not reached within $n$ steps.
nodes.title: Path recovered from an A-star result

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with natural edge weights $w$, let $h$ be a consistent heuristic with natural values, and let $w_h(x, y) = w(x, y) + h(y) - h(x)$ be the reduced weight, with the subtraction truncated at $0$. For all vertices $u$ and $v$ and every nonempty list of vertices $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_k$ with $v_0 = u$, $v_k = v$ and an edge of $G$ from each $v_i$ to $v_{i+1}$,…
nodes.title: Reduced weights telescope along paths

nodes.summary: Let $w$ assign a natural number $w(u, v)$ to each pair of vertices and let $h$ assign a natural number to each vertex. The reduced weight of the pair $(u, v)$ is the natural number $w(u, v) + h(v) - h(u)$, computed with truncated subtraction, so it is $0$ when $h(u) > w(u, v) + h(v)$.
nodes.title: Reduced weight

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
